snapshot: WHO Western Pacific Region. Domestic health policy is dominated by the repair of regional and essential care after the 2024 to 2025 doctors' dispute, alongside medical AI and an ageing population.

agenda.title: Regional and essential healthcare
agenda.text: In the second-half work plan presented to President Lee on 16 July 2026, the ministry set out a special fund of KRW 1.2 trillion per year, within KRW 3.6 trillion per year for regional and essential care through an overhaul of health insurance fees. It aims to save KRW 2.6 trillion a year by curbing excessive imaging and specimen tests, and to raise regional emergency medical centres to as many as 60.

agenda.title: Medical AI and bio growth
agenda.text: An AI Basic Medical Strategy was due that month, together with a platform for sharing medical images to avoid repeated CT and MRI scans. Bio and AI are named as growth engines in the plan.

agenda.title: Welfare and pension reform
agenda.text: The plan moves to proactive welfare, with automatic child allowances and small emergency living expenses for households in crisis, and to a restructured basic pension. Suicide-prevention counselling staff are to rise from 103 to 200.
